chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Dawud from Ali ibn Habashi ibn Quniyy who said: Ali ibn Sulayman al-Zurari narrated to us from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Khaybari from Yazid ibn Abd al-Malik from his father from his grandfather who said:

I entered upon Fatimah (peace be upon her), and she initiated me with the greeting of peace, then she said, 'What has brought you?' I said, 'Seeking blessings.' She said, 'My father informed me, and he is as he is, that whoever greets him and me for three days, Allah has made Paradise obligatory for him.' I said to her, 'During his life and your life?' She said, 'Yes, and after our death.' And as for the words said upon visiting her (peace be upon her), it has been narrated.

key_terms.أَوْجَبَ اللَّهُ لَهُ الْجَنَّةَ: Allah has made Paradise obligatory for him
key_terms.فَاطِمَةُ عَلَيْهَا السَّلَامُ: Fatimah (peace be upon her), daughter of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for greeting Prophet Muhammad and Fatimah for three days?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the grandfather of the narrator encounters Fatimah al-Zahra (peace be upon her), who reveals a specific virtue: greeting both her and the Prophet Muhammad for three days guarantees Paradise. This ruling is explicitly stated to apply both during their lifetimes and after their death, establishing the enduring spiritual efficacy of salutations directed to the Ahl al-Bayt. The hadith underscores the unique status of Fatimah as a conduit of divine blessing, linking her intercessory role directly to the Prophet's own authority.
